title: fMRI Anticipation vs. Experience Study: Dissociating Somatic Marker Retrieval from Prediction Error
description: Event-related risk-decision fMRI dissociates anticipatory value-related vmPFC/aINS coupling from outcome-related interoceptive error, with orthogonal cue contrast and long versus zero foreperiod controls.

sub_predictions.claim: vmPFC BOLD modulated by EV during anticipation but does not correlate with outcome-locked SCR
sub_predictions.confirming_evidence: vmPFC anticipation-period BOLD modulated by EV (p < 0.05 FWE); vmPFC–SCR outcome correlation r < 0.2
sub_predictions.falsifying_evidence: vmPFC BOLD is NOT modulated by EV during anticipation (effect p > 0.10, fails the positive conjunct); OR vmPFC BOLD correlates significantly with outcome-locked SCR (r > 0.35, fails the null conjunct)
sub_predictions.indeterminate_rule: Failure to confirm alone is not evidence of falsification. Apply the registered interval/evidence rule and admissibility gate.

sub_predictions.claim: vmPFC→aINS connectivity peaks during emotional anticipation (precision-gain pathway M̂ → β_SM → Πⁱ_eff) while vmPFC→pIC connectivity remains statistically flat (sensory-intensity pathway, unmodulated by M̂). This within-study dissociation is the operational test that M̂ acts on precision gain, not error magnitude.

inclusion_criteria: Participants eligible for MRI and individually calibrated aversive task under approved protocol.
exclusion_criteria: Insufficient admissible trials or motion quality
Maximum tolerated calibrated shock below 1.5 mA: exclude interoceptive-error analyses and report separately.

apparatus.fMRI: 3T, 64 slices, 2 mm isotropic, TR1000/TE30 ms, multiband4
apparatus.stressor: Individually calibrated shock versus mild vibration under approved protocol
apparatus.vmPFC_roi: NeuroVault collection917 image13359, mask SHA256 required; image13347 and AAL2 as sensitivity
apparatus.pIC_roi: Faillenot probabilistic posterior-insula atlas; not unsplit AAL2 insula

target.type: High/low-risk choices with >=4 expected-value levels and orthogonal visual cue contrast

trial_structure.response: Choice, decision RT and anticipatory anxiety rating 1–7

primary_hypothesis: Anticipatory vmPFC value coding and aINS coupling dissociate from outcome SCR/pIC and cue contrast, and aINS coupling declines in the zero-foreperiod condition.
primary_analysis: Event-related GLM and PPI with small-volume FWE; three prespecified ROIs, 24 motion regressors, RETROICOR and RT. All tests two-tailed. Anticipation-versus-outcome aINS PPI is the powered primary contrast (Pred 3.B in detailed registry); anticipatory SCR correlation and beta_SM trait estimates are secondary/exploratory.

power_analysis.assumption_status: Working effect-size assumption; sensitivity simulation required.

apgi_parameters.model: Reduced empirical specification: seven core quantities plus somatic modulation; not eight freely fitted parameters in every dataset.

gamma_sig.role: population-fixed model sigmoid steepness; distinct from alpha_psy

beta_SM.role: somatic modulation gain; not independently identifiable from Pi_i using behavior alone

kappa.role: energy-information bridge only; never ignition steepness

apgi_parameters.gain_interpretation: Pi_i in the reduced confirmatory model is salience-weighted gain; HEP is a candidate indicator, not a direct inverse-variance measurement.
apgi_parameters.accumulation: S_next=(1-a_S)*S+a_S*u; a_S=1-exp(-dt/tau_S); u uses calibration-fixed relative gains and excess magnitudes abs(z)-sqrt(2/pi).
apgi_parameters.ignition: p_k=1-exp(-r_max*sigmoid(gamma_sig*(S-theta))*dt); single trial-window sigmoid sampling is a distinct convention, never interchanged within a protocol.
apgi_parameters.time_step: dt=0.01 s reduced reference; dt<=min(tau_S,tau_theta,tau_Pi)/10; active reservoir additionally requires dt<=tau_res/10.
apgi_parameters.parameter_manifest_status: Required before confirmatory fitting; no unspecified coefficient is assigned a legacy default.

quality_and_decision_rules.data_admissibility: Apply registered quality gates before inference. Inadmissible data are exploratory, receive no Scenario A–F, and carry no framework vote.

scenarios.A: Scenario A — Confirmed. p < α and BF₁₀ ≥ 100. Both streams converge on H₁. Counted toward framework-level BY-FDR confirmation and toward the joint Bayesian meta-analysis. No additional replication is required before the claim is filed.
scenarios.B: Scenario B — Tentative confirmation. p < α and 3 ≤ BF₁₀ < 100. The frequentist threshold is met but Bayesian evidence is moderate rather than strong; reported as "frequentist-significant, Bayesian moderate." One pre-registered independent replication is required before the result is elevated to confirmatory status, and that replication is registered before the primary result is published.
scenarios.C: Scenario C — Discordant (frequentist-positive, Bayesian-null). p < α and BF₁₀ < 3. The frequentist threshold is met but the Bayes factor provides less than moderate evidence for H₁ and may favor H₀. Classified as equivocal: the result neither confirms nor falsifies the prediction. It is flagged as equivocal in the results and recorded in the analysis log (not in the protocol-deviation register, which is reserved for departures from registered procedure). Independent replication at ≥ 90% power is required before any interpretation is made.
scenarios.D: Scenario D — Bayesian positive (without frequentist significance). p ≥ α and BF₁₀ ≥ 100. Strong probabilistic support for H₁ while the NHST threshold is missed. Not counted toward BY-FDR (which operates on the frequentist p-values). The original study plus one pre-registered replication are required for elevation to confirmatory status.
scenarios.E: Scenario E — Bayesian falsification. p ≥ α and BF₀₁ ≥ 6. The frequentist result is nonsignificant and the Bayesian analysis supports H₀. Classified as provisional falsification of the specific sub-prediction and reported as such in the primary manuscript. A single Scenario E result triggers independent replication at ≥ 90% power before the sub-prediction is declared definitively falsified, and triggers review of whether the framework-level falsification threshold has been reached (two or more Scenario E results across primary protocols; framework-level decision rule).
scenarios.F: Scenario F — Indeterminate. p ≥ α and 1/6 < BF₁₀ < 100 (i.e., neither BF₁₀ ≥ 100 nor BF₀₁ ≥ 6). Neither stream reaches a decision threshold. Classified as inconclusive: it carries no confirmatory or falsifying weight and is reported transparently as indeterminate. It may motivate a pre-registered replication but does not by itself trigger one, and it is never counted toward BY-FDR confirmation or framework-level falsification.

quality_and_decision_rules.framework_confirmation: At least 4/5 primary protocols, combined hierarchical BF10>=100, and at most one Scenario E protocol. Protocol 0 is a gate; 2 contributes F2; 6 is CE.
quality_and_decision_rules.protocol_alpha_specification: Protocol 3 (Anticipation-fMRI): Cluster FWE z > 3.1, p < 0.05. Small-volume FWE for ROIs. All primary tests are two-tailed.
quality_and_decision_rules.decision_precedence: Prediction-specific estimands, interval/evidence rules and admissibility gates govern over abbreviated source summaries. The A–F matrix applies only where both frequentist and Bayesian hypotheses are explicitly defined; do not invent a point-null Bayes factor. Nonsignificance or a point estimate alone does not establish equivalence or falsification; specificity requires a direct contrast. Unresolved interval bounds or multiplicity allocations require prospective analysis lock.

specification_sections.heading: Dissociating Somatic Marker Retrieval from Prediction Error
specification_sections.text: Protocol 3 (Anticipation-fMRI) dissociates somatic marker retrieval (M) in anticipation from primary interoceptive prediction error (εⁱ) in experience, and tests individual differences in somatic-marker gain β_SM.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Task Design
specification_sections.text: Protocol 3 (Anticipation-fMRI) uses event-related fMRI during a decision-making task in which participants choose between a high-risk deck (high monetary reward paired with painful electric shock, 2–4 mA) and a low-risk deck (low monetary reward paired with mild vibration). Option expected value varies across ≥ 4 levels (reward magnitude × shock probability) so that the EV regressor in Pred 3.A and Pred 3.C is parametric; the luminance contrast of the option cue is varied orthogonally to EV, providing the sensory-contrast regressor for Pred 3.C. The aversive somatic stressor is methodologically essential: cutaneous electric shock engages nociceptive–interoceptive pathways to the insula (Craig, 2009) and generates bodily prediction errors (εⁱ) rather than abstract reward signals, which would engage a different precision-weighting system and collapse the distinction between APGI and standard reinforcement learning. Individual pain thresholds are calibrated before scanning to equate subjective intensity across participants.

specification_sections.heading: Parameter Identifiability Pre-Check (required before main analysis)
specification_sections.text:
Identifiability of β_SM (somatic modulation gain) and Πⁱ (interoceptive precision) is confirmed prior to main Protocol 3 (Anticipation-fMRI) analysis via a pre-session protocol using alternating fMRI and SCR-only blocks to estimate the two parameters from orthogonal measurement channels.

Criterion: Use the same scaled, dimensionless identifiability diagnostic as Protocol 2: R_ij = I_ij/√(I_ii I_jj) and max |R_ij| < 0.1 for the β_SM–Πⁱ block. Signed or raw off-diagonal entries are not the criterion. If the criterion is unmet, individual parameter claims are exploratory and confirmatory fitting follows only the prospectively specified composite-parameter model. The evaluation grid and scaled condition-number criterion are archived before analysis.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Shock protocol integrity
specification_sections.text: Two additional specifications are required to prevent M(c,a) signal confounds. First, a minimum inter-trial interval of 8 seconds (within the pre-specified 6–10 s jittered ITI range) will be enforced following any high-risk trial receiving shock delivery, to allow SCR return to baseline and prevent allostatic sensitization of the interoceptive signal across consecutive trials. Second, if a participant reports pain intensity > 7/10 on any trial during the calibration phase, shock intensity will be reduced by 0.5 mA and recalibrated; sessions in which maximum tolerated intensity falls below 1.5 mA (insufficient to generate reliable SCR) will be excluded from the interoceptive prediction error analyses and reported separately.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Sample size rationale
specification_sections.text: The confirmatory basis is the within-subject vmPFC→aINS PPI contrast (anticipation vs. outcome; paired t, two-tailed). No directly relevant vmPFC–aINS PPI effect-size anchor is established here; d = 0.50 is a conservative working design assumption requiring simulation and sensitivity analysis. Conservative power calculation at d = 0.50, α = 0.05 (two-tailed), power = 0.80 yields N ≈ 34 analyzable participants; we adopt N = 36 as the required analyzable sample. Enrollment targets N = 40 to retain N = 36 after ~10% motion exclusion. N = 36 analyzable is the minimum; no smaller analyzable sample is admissible. This confirmatory test is powered at 80% for d ≈ 0.50 only; smaller true effects (d < 0.40) will be under-powered. The correlational analysis (vmPFC anticipatory BOLD × SCR/d′, r = 0.40) is powered at ≈ 0.68 at N = 36 and is designated secondary, not confirmatory; a confirmatory correlational test at 90% power would require N ≈ 62. All Protocol 3 tests are two-tailed. The exploratory β_SM analysis (somatic influence gain; Protocol 3 exploratory analysis (ii)) uses the available N = 36; its power is not established by Critchley et al. (2004), whose design does not provide a directly matched effect-size anchor. Effect estimates and uncertainty are reported, and any analysis-specific sensitivity simulation is archived.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Trial timing
specification_sections.text: Decision: 4 s (anticipation/M(c,a) retrieval phase) with foreperiod length manipulated within-session (0 ms vs 2000–4000 ms jittered, blocked within runs and counterbalanced across participants), outcome 2 s (experience/εⁱ generation phase), jittered ITI 6–10 s. Measures include fMRI BOLD from vmPFC, amygdala, anterior insula, posterior insula and ACC; skin conductance response (SCR) with anticipatory peaks during decisions; and subjective anxiety ratings (1–7 scale) during anticipation.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Trial counts
specification_sections.text: Each run comprises 100 trials (50 high-risk, 50 low-risk; half with the long foreperiod, blocked within run) across two runs = 200 decision trials per participant, giving ≥ 25 high-risk long-foreperiod trials per run (§3.1.3). The 4 s anticipation window provides sufficient temporal resolution for vmPFC BOLD modeling; the 6–10 s jittered ITI ensures adequate baseline estimation. This trial count yields 25 trials per risk-by-foreperiod condition per run for first-level beta estimation, consistent with fMRI decision-neuroscience standards (cf. Rangel & Hare, 2010).
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: fMRI acquisition parameters
specification_sections.text: Event-related design, TR = 1.0 s, TE = 30 ms, flip angle 78°, 64 slices (2 mm isotropic), multiband factor 4. Slice-timing correction referenced to middle slice. Total run duration: 2 runs × ≈ 26 min = ≈ 52 min. Field maps acquired for each run for distortion correction. GLM first-level models will include the 24 motion parameters of §4.2.2, cardiac and respiratory regressors (RETROICOR), and trial-by-trial RT as a nuisance regressor. These specifications are targets; any scanner-specific deviations will be logged as pre-registration amendments.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 3.A — vmPFC–insula anticipatory coupling
specification_sections.text: vmPFC BOLD during the anticipation foreperiod is parametrically modulated by option expected value (p < 0.05 FWE, small-volume) and does not correlate with outcome-locked SCR (r < 0.20) — the two conjuncts of Pred 3.A (Table 7). The anticipatory vmPFC–SCR correlation (r ≈ 0.40) is a secondary analysis (power ≈ 0.68). The hypothesized vmPFC-to-autonomic timing is a latent neural sequence, not a claim that observed vmPFC BOLD peaks 1–2 s after decision onset. Temporal analyses are exploratory unless the HRF/deconvolution model, event timing, lag estimator and uncertainty procedure are locked before acquisition. The PPI contrast does not establish millisecond directionality.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 3.B — vmPFC→aINS anticipatory coupling; vmPFC→pIC flat (PPI dissociation)
specification_sections.text: vmPFC→aINS PPI coupling is greater during the anticipation foreperiod than in the outcome window (p < 0.05 FWE, Δr ≥ 0.30), whereas vmPFC→pIC coupling does not change (BF₀₁ ≥ 6) — the within-study dissociation of precision gain (aINS) from error magnitude (pIC). The experience-phase vmPFC–pIC null and the pIC–pain-rating correlation are exploratory (Protocol 3 exploratory analysis (i)).
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 3.C — Context-specific: vmPFC modulated by valence, not sensory contrast
specification_sections.text: vmPFC BOLD during anticipation is parametrically modulated by option expected value (valence), not by sensory contrast: the anticipatory vmPFC response scales with deck valence at matched sensory contrast. The anxiety→vmPFC–aINS coupling / β_SM individual-differences analysis is reported separately as Protocol 3 exploratory analysis (ii).
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 3.D — No-foreperiod (0 ms) control collapses vmPFC→aINS anticipatory coupling
specification_sections.text: vmPFC→aINS anticipatory coupling is present under a long foreperiod (2000–4000 ms) and abolished under the 0-ms no-foreperiod control, dissociating anticipatory Πⁱ_eff retrieval from outcome-locked εⁱ encoding. The learning-curve analysis (steeper vmPFC slopes for pain vs monetary outcomes) is reported separately as Protocol 3 exploratory analysis (iii).
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Control Analyses
specification_sections.text: Motion correction and physiological noise removal (RETROICOR); individual pain thresholds calibrated pre-scan; trial-by-trial regressors for decision time (RT) to control speed-accuracy trade-offs.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Exploratory Extensions (non-confirmatory)
specification_sections.text: The confirmatory Protocol 3 codes 3.A–3.D are defined identically in the companion Protocols document; this Preregistration governs. Three additional analyses are designated exploratory and do not gate framework-level assessment: (i) experience-phase vmPFC–pIC null (r < 0.20) with pIC–pain-intensity r > 0.50 confirming pIC as the active εⁱ generator; (ii) trait differences in somatic-influence gain (β_SM individual-differences analysis; N ≈ 28–36); (iii) interoceptive salience accelerating somatic-marker learning (steeper vmPFC learning curves for pain vs. monetary outcomes). These analyses are not registered predictions, carry no prediction code and do not share an estimand with Pred 3.B, 3.C or 3.D.

methods_source_sections.heading: Outliers and influence
methods_source_sections.text:
4.3.2 Outlier and influential-observation policy

All rules below are fixed pre-collection and apply to every protocol unless a protocol body specifies otherwise; no post-hoc outlier rule may be introduced. (a) Trial level. Scalp-EEG trials exceeding the 150 µV peak-to-peak criterion (§4.2.1) are rejected; iEEG trials follow the interictal-discharge and |z| > 6 rule of §Protocol 6; behavioral trials in speeded detection tasks with RT < 150 ms or > 3 s are rejected as anticipations or lapses (Protocol 2 IGT and Protocol 7 bedside tasks use the rules in their protocol bodies). No further trial-level trimming is permitted. (b) Participant level. A participant is excluded only for a pre-registered admissibility failure (> 30% trial rejection, Data-Admissibility Gate; failed manipulation check; protocol violation). Statistical outlyingness is never itself an exclusion ground. (c) Observation level in models. Continuous predictors and outcomes are winsorized at ±3 SD within participant before entry into any confirmatory model; the untrimmed analysis is reported alongside as a mandatory sensitivity analysis, and a discrepancy in the confirmatory decision between the two is reported as an instability flag. (d) Influence. For every confirmatory regression or mixed model, Cook's distance is computed and observations with D > 4/n are reported; the model is refit without them as a sensitivity analysis. The trimmed refit is never the confirmatory result. (e) Model diagnostics and fallback. Gaussian models use the registered residual diagnostics; binary/ordinal generalized models use distribution-appropriate simulation or predictive diagnostics, not a Shapiro–Wilk residual gate. Appendix C must identify the exact estimator, tuning constants, inferential test and Bayesian evidence computation for each permitted fallback before lock. A fallback not so specified is a sensitivity analysis and cannot replace the primary confirmatory estimator.

methods_source_sections.heading: Bayesian prior sensitivity
methods_source_sections.text:
Sensitivity analyses

All confirmatory Bayesian conclusions are re-run under fixed prior transformations. Normal and HalfNormal priors: scale multiplied by 2 and by ½, location and support unchanged. Beta(2, 5) prior on η_RL: mean (2/7) preserved and concentration (sum of shape parameters, 7) multiplied by 2 and by ½, giving Beta(4, 10) and Beta(1, 2.5). Fixed parameters remain fixed or vary over a separately registered grid. Every evidence and interval criterion is recomputed under each sensitivity prior; if a conclusion crosses a §3.5.2 decision boundary (BF₁₀ = 3 or 100, BF₀₁ = 6), it is reported as prior-sensitive and reclassified as exploratory.

methods_source_sections.heading: Protocol-specific ethics and regulatory source
methods_source_sections.text:
Protocol 3 (Anticipation-fMRI)

Status: Ethics approval pending at time of registration lock.
Committee: Protocol is registered as a planned study and the registration will be amended with committee name, institution, approval number and date before any participant is approached.
Stimulation: Electric shock (individually calibrated, typically 2–4 mA; 1.5 mA floor). Participants receive threshold calibration; shock amplitude adjusted to individual tolerance.
Informed consent: Explicit disclosure of shock stimulation with opportunity to withdraw at any point.
